hook.situation: After class, a friend asks what the teacher said. You need to pass along a statement, a question, and an instruction without mixing the endings.
objectives: Report statements with -다고 했어요 and recognize the spoken contraction -대요.
Use -는지 when a question is embedded inside 알다, 모르다, 확인하다, or 궁금하다.
hook.whyItMatters: Reported speech is not one pattern. Korean changes the ending depending on what the original sentence was: a statement, a question, or an instruction.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-다고 했어요 — Reporting what someone said
grammarNotes.func: Use -다고 했어요 to report a statement someone made, like English "said that …". You report the meaning, not the exact words, so you drop the original ending (요/-어) and attach -다고 to the plain stem.

formTable.when: Action verb, present — stem ends in a vowel
Action verb, present — stem ends in a 받침

formTable.ex: 바쁘다 → 바쁘다고 했어요 / 좋다 → 좋다고 했어요
먹었다 → 먹었다고 했어요 / 갔다 → 갔다고 했어요
학생 → 학생이라고 했어요 / 친구 → 친구라고 했어요

examples.ko: 친구가 내일 학교에 안 온다고 했어요.
examples.romanization: chinguga naeil hakgyoe an ondago haesseoyo.
examples.en: My friend said he won't come to school tomorrow.
examples.note: 오다 is an action verb, so present is 온다고, not 오다고.
Past tense: keep 먹었- and add -다고. The past never takes -ㄴ다고/-는다고.

examples.en: The teacher said Korean isn't hard.
examples.note: 어렵다 is an adjective, so just -다고 — no -ㄴ-/-는-.
Noun + 이다 becomes (이)라고. 친구 ends in a vowel, so 친구라고.

keyPoint.label: Verbs vs. adjectives in the present
keyPoint.body: Only action verbs add -ㄴ다고/-는다고 (간다고, 먹는다고). Adjectives, and all past forms, just add -다고 (바쁘다고, 먹었다고). The common slips are 먹다고 (should be 먹는다고) and 바쁜다고 (should be 바쁘다고).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 먹는다고 the ㄱ before ㄴ turns into an ㅇ sound, so it comes out [멍는다고].

drill.instruction: Report what each person said using -다고 했어요. Watch verb vs. adjective and tense.
drill.model: 민수: "시간이 없어요." → 민수가 시간이 없다고 했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: In English you just add "that," so it's tempting to glue -다고 onto the dictionary form 오다. But present-tense action verbs need -ㄴ다고/-는다고: 오다 → 온다고.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-냐고 물어봤어요 — Reporting a question
grammarNotes.func: Use -냐고 물어봤어요 (or 물었어요) to report a question someone asked — "someone asked whether/what …". The reported part ends in -냐고 no matter how polite the original question was.

examples.en: My friend asked me whether I'd eaten.
examples.note: Past yes/no question → -었냐고. 한테 marks the person who was asked.

examples.en: The teacher asked the students whether they had time.
examples.note: 있다 → 있냐고. A yes/no question with no question word.

examples.en: Mom asked where I was going.
examples.note: The question word 어디 stays where it is — Korean doesn't move it to the front.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 제가 한국 사람이냐고 물어봤어요.
examples.romanization: geu sarami jega hanguk saraminyago mureobwasseoyo.
examples.en: That person asked whether I was Korean.
examples.note: Noun + 이다 → 이냐고. The subject inside the quote takes 가/이 (제가), not 는.

keyPoint.label: -다고 vs. -냐고
keyPoint.body: Statements use -다고 했어요; questions use -냐고 물어봤어요. The following verb is your clue: 했어요/말했어요 (said) for statements, 물어봤어요/물었어요 (asked) for questions.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 먹었냐고 the ㅆ받침 before ㄴ becomes an ㄴ sound, so it links as [머건냐고].

drill.instruction: Report each question with -냐고 물어봤어요. Keep any question word in place.
drill.model: 엄마: "숙제 다 했어?" → 엄마가 숙제 다 했냐고 물어봤어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners reuse the statement ending -다고 with 물어봤어요. But a reported question has to end in -냐고; -다고 only goes with 했어요/말했어요.

grammarNotes.title: V-는지 / A-(으)ㄴ지 / N인지 — "whether / what / where …" inside a sentence
grammarNotes.func: Use -는지/-(으)ㄴ지/-인지 to tuck a question inside a bigger sentence — "I don't know whether/what/where …", "Do you know if …?". It turns the question into a clause that then connects to verbs like 알다, 모르다, 궁금하다.

examples.en: I don't know where my friend lives.
examples.note: 살다 drops the ㄹ before -는지 → 사는지. 어디 stays inside the clause.

examples.en: I wonder whether this movie is good.
examples.note: 재미있다 takes -는지 (not -(으)ㄴ지) because of the 있다 part.

examples.en: I'm not sure whether he finished eating.
examples.note: Past → -었는지. 모르겠어요 sounds softer than 몰라요, more like "I'm not sure."

examples.en: Do you know who that person is?
examples.note: 누구 + 이다 → 누구인지. It pairs naturally with 알다/아세요.

keyPoint.label: Adjective -(으)ㄴ지 vs. verb -는지
keyPoint.body: In the present, adjectives take -(으)ㄴ지 (좋은지, 바쁜지) and action verbs take -는지 (가는지, 먹는지). In the past, both use -았/었는지 (좋았는지, 갔는지), so the split only matters in the present.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 먹는지 comes out [멍는지] (ㄱ → ㅇ before ㄴ); in 좋은지 the ㅎ drops, so it sounds like [조은지].

drill.instruction: Finish each sentence with -는지/-(으)ㄴ지/-인지. Watch verb vs. adjective and tense.
drill.model: (친구가 오다) 친구가 ___ 모르겠어요. → 친구가 오는지 모르겠어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 재미있다/맛있다/없다 look like adjectives, but the 있/없 part acts like a verb and takes -는지, not -(으)ㄴ지. So it's 재미있는지, 맛있는지, 없는지.

exampleSentence.en: The teacher said we will take it on Friday.
My friend asked what time we are meeting.
Do you know when the exam is?
The teacher told us to submit the homework.
The teacher says the exam is on Friday.

extendedVocabulary.english: to ask; to ask and find out

exampleSentence.en: I asked my friend when the exam is.

exampleSentence.ko: 잘 못 들었으면 다시 말해 달라고 해요.
exampleSentence.en: If you did not hear it well, ask them to say it again.
exampleSentence.note: Useful repair phrase when reported information is unclear.

exampleSentence.en: They told us to submit the homework by tomorrow.
Do you know when the exam is?
They asked whether I submitted the homework.
exampleSentence.note: A practical school/work verb for reported questions.

exampleSentence.en: Please check what time we are meeting.
I will pass the details on to my friend.
exampleSentence.note: The communication job of reported speech.

extendedDialogue.setting: A classmate passes along what the teacher said after class.

readingText.title: 선생님이 뭐라고 하셨어요?
readingText.body: 수업이 끝난 뒤 친구에게 내용을 전할 때는 원래 문장이 어떤 종류였는지 먼저 봐야 해요. 선생님이 '금요일에 시험을 봐요'라고 말한 내용은 '금요일에 본다고 하셨어요'로 전할 수 있어요. 질문을 전할 때는 '-냐고'를 써요. 그래서 '몇 시에 만나요?'는 '몇 시에 만나냐고 물어봤어요'가 돼요. 하지만 누가 질문한 것이 아니라 내가 답을 알고 싶은 상황이면 '-는지'가 자연스러워요. '시험이 언제인지 알아요?'처럼 큰 문장 안에 질문을 넣는 거예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When passing along class information, first identify the original sentence type. Statements use -다고 했어요, questions use -냐고 물어봤어요, and embedded questions use -는지 inside verbs like know, not know, or check.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 원래 문장이 statement이면 어떤 표현을 써요?
질문을 전할 때는 어떤 표현을 써요?
큰 문장 안에 질문을 넣을 때는 어떤 표현을 써요?

culturalNote.title: The ending carries the original sentence type
culturalNote.body: In Korean, the listener can often tell whether the original was a statement, question, or instruction from the reported ending itself. That is why choosing -다고, -냐고, or -(으)라고 matters.
culturalNote.tip: Before reporting someone else's words, label the source sentence: statement, question, or instruction.

inlineExercises.prompt: The teacher said, '금요일에 시험을 봐요.' Which report is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: The original is a statement, so use -다고 하셨어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Your friend asked, '몇 시에 만나요?' Which report is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: The original is a question, so use -냐고 물어봤어요.
알다 takes the embedded question form -는지/-인지.

inlineExercises.prompt: 선생님___ 숙제를 제출하라고 하셨어요. (The teacher told us to submit homework.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 선생님 is the respected subject who gave the instruction, so use 께서. 께 would mark a recipient instead.
Action verbs use -ㄴ/는다고 for reported statements. 보다 becomes 본다고 했어요 in this sentence.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'My friend asked what time we meet.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Reported questions use -냐고 물어봤어요. The embedded question keeps 몇 시에 inside the reported content.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'Please check whether there is homework.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -는지 embeds the question inside 확인하다. 숙제가 있는지 means whether homework exists.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the report: '친구가 몇 시에 만나다고 물어봤어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: A reported question needs -냐고, not -다고. -다고 reports a statement.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which is the spoken short form of 선생님이 내일 시험이 있다고 했어요?
inlineExercises.explanation: -대요 is the common spoken contraction for “they say that.” 있냐고요 would report or repeat a question.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'I don't know whether there is an exam.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -는지 works inside 모르다 for an embedded question. 시험이 있는지 means whether there is an exam.

bullets: Embedded questions: -는지 with 알다, 모르다, 확인하다, 궁금하다.

writingTask.prompt: Message a classmate to relay what the teacher announced today: what the teacher said about the homework, and what a classmate asked you about it.
writingTask.hint: Report a statement with -다고 했어요 (제출하라고 했어요 / 어렵다고 했어요), report a question with -냐고 물어봤어요, and embed a question with -는지 (언제까지인지 몰라서).
writingTask.model: 선생님이 오늘 숙제를 금요일까지 제출하라고 했어요. 그리고 시험이 어렵다고 했어요. 민수 씨가 저한테 숙제가 언제까지냐고 물어봤는데, 저도 정확히 언제까지인지 몰라서 다시 확인했어요.
writingTask.modelEn: The teacher said today to submit the homework by Friday. And said the exam is hard. Minsu asked me when the homework is due, but I didn't know exactly when it was due either, so I checked again.

canDo: Pass along what someone said with -다고 했어요 (어렵다고 했어요)
Relay an order with -(으)라고 하다 (제출하라고 했어요)
Report a question someone asked with -냐고 물어봤어요
Tuck a question inside a sentence with -는지/-(으)ㄴ지 (언제까지인지 몰라요)
